findings.title: Near-miss rule did not ripple to its carriers — task gloss contradicts the tightened legacy definition
findings.recommendation: Task 1.1 still says 'legacy docs (zero parseable stages) yield an explicit legacy/opaque result, never an error' — the superseded definition; under the near-miss rule a doc whose only heading is malformed has zero parseable stages yet must be a validation error/malformed listing. No carrier names the near-miss behaviors (1.1 parser distinction, 1.3 status malformed listing, 1.4 malformed+slotless fixtures, design D1). Reword 1.1's parenthetical to the outside-fences definition + near-miss result; add fixtures to 1.4; note malformed listing in 1.3; one line in design D1.

findings.title: Un-delta'd baseline claim — 'the entire orbit/explore/<name>/ directory is moved' falsified by the metadata merge
findings.recommendation: The staging-directory requirement's Promoted-via-propose scenario asserts the ENTIRE directory moves; under the ratified merge semantics the staged .openspec.yaml is merged then DISCARDED, never moved. Add a 4th conventions MODIFIED block amending the scenario (entire directory except .openspec.yaml, which merges per orbit-propose-modifications; optionally note the Mode B metadata file in the created-by-explore scenario); stamp the 16th fingerprint.

findings.title: Zero-parseable-docs status scenario collides with malformed/legacy listing semantics
findings.recommendation: The scenario's WHEN covers malformed-only/legacy-only repos but its THEN demands the clean no-docs message with an empty --json list, contradicting the malformed listing (near-miss rule) and legacy listing. Scope the scenario to no-architecture-docs-at-all, or define the --json shape as bucketed (parseable/legacy/malformed) with 'empty' meaning the parseable bucket.

findings.title: Architecture-mode target scenario conflates malformed docs with legacy
findings.recommendation: 'legacy (zero-parseable-stage) doc is an error suggesting retrofit' uses the pre-near-miss equation. Reword: legacy doc -> error suggesting retrofit; doc failing orbit architecture validate (malformed) -> error naming the violation.

findings.title: Arc charter's state-vocabulary sketch says 'archived'; D-d2-1 ratified quiescent
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the charter's 'archived (archive back-reference)' to quiescent (or add a superseded-by-D-d2-1 note) during the task 3.1 retrofit so the day-one architecture review doesn't flag it. Editorial only (charter prose is engine-opaque).

findings.title: Verb-taxonomy new-verb justification letter not explicitly satisfied for architect
findings.recommendation: One sentence in design D6: 'architect is a new authoring-genre verb, justified by D-d2-6/R-d-1' — closes the orbit-conventions verb-taxonomy requirement's letter cheaply.
